holidays.name: National Superhero Day
holidays.description: Break out the capes and masks. This is the day to celebrate caped crusaders, web-slingers and everyday heroes. Binge a hero movie marathon, dress up like your favorite champion, or thank a real-life hero in your neighborhood.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance that grew out of comic book and pop culture fandom. It's popularly credited to Marvel Comics, which promoted it in the early 2000s.
holidays.funFact: Many classic superheroes have secret identities with ordinary jobs, such as reporters, students and scientists. That's a nice reminder that heroes can look like anyone.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Pie Day
holidays.description: A day for flaky crust, jammy purple filling and a big scoop of vanilla ice cream on the side. Bake one from scratch or treat yourself to a slice. Your fork will come away stained, and that's part of the fun.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food holiday that honors one of America's favorite fruit pies. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America. They were a staple for Indigenous peoples long before they ended up in pies.

holidays.name: National Great Poetry Reading Day
holidays.description: Pick up a poem and read it out loud, whether to a friend, a pet or your bathroom mirror. Poetry is meant to be heard, so dramatic voices are encouraged. Hosting an impromptu open mic is a bonus.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance that encourages people to share and enjoy poetry. Its origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Poetry is among the oldest art forms. Many early poems were passed down by memory and performance long before they were written down.
